relevance_note: Single case report of a man with two ABCA1 variants: "A heterozygous missense variant of ABCA1 (ATP binding cassette transporter A1) gene, [NM_005502.3] c.103A>G (p.Ile35Val) along with another heterozygous nonsense mutation c.679C>T (p.Arg227Ter) were detected."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans/fields. Scope: the proband ('patient', rule 5; 'proband' is a role word) plus four relatives described in relation to him: mother (affected, MI, deceased; not tested), elder sister and 2 adolescent children (not genetically tested, but lipid-tested with HDL >40 mg/dL). No variant rows for relatives (none genetically tested). Zygosity: Results call each variant 'heterozygous'; the Discussion states 'the patient had compound heterozygous variants'. Phase was not shown (mother untested, no other relatives tested); recorded the authors' 'compound heterozygous' with both spans. Transcript NM_005502.3 is printed only before c.103A>G; not copied to c.679C>T. In-silico predictions (DANN, LRT, MetaLR, GERP) are not functional assays, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Abstract's 'a possibly pathogenic variant of ABCA1 gene' does not say which variant; pathogenicity taken from the Discussion. Ages: '41-year-old' is the age at first visit in June 2011, not at last evaluation (patient returned in 2019, age not given), so age at last evaluation is not reported; onset of MIs is given only as a year ('since 2012'), so age at onset not reported. 'without ... organomegaly' was read as excluding splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on examination. Mother's MI was not taken as 'coronary artery disease' on the checklist (not stated as such). Table 1 values were used only where the text interprets them (homocysteine, Protein C) or the cell states 'Absent' (lupus anticoagulant); other values within or outside the printed normal range (e.g. anti-TPO 112 vs <100, platelets 1.5 lakhs at the lower limit, LDL and triglycerides in Table 2) were not turned into features. The antiphospholipid antibody row is garbled in the conversion ('1.83.7' / '<10<10') and was not used. Internal inconsistency noted: Table 2 and the text show HDL below 40 mg/dL at every time point (30, 5, 24; otherwise 15-38), whereas the Discussion says 'HDL levels being marginally low only once' and the conclusion says 'low-normal HDL levels'; low HDL recorded as observed from the data and the abstract ('mildly reduced HDL'). 'None of the extended family members had any cardiovascular event' was not applied to the sister or children (extended family not named as including them).
